newsitem.title: USA: Aetna outlines terms for president.
newsitem.headline: Aetna outlines terms for president.

text.p: Healthcare and life insurer Aetna Inc will pay its new president more than $2 million if he is not named chief executive within a year, the company said in recent federal filings.
Joseph Sebastianelli, 50, was named president in March of this year.

Aetna said if he is not offered the chief executive's post by February 28, 1998, and quits within a year of that date, he will get severance equal to three times his base salary and target annual bonus.
Sebastianelli and Richard L. Huber, Aetna vice chairman for strategy and finance, are considered by analysts to be the top contenders to succeed Chairman and Chief Executive Ronald Compton.
Compton has said he plans to retire when he turns 65 next February.
Aetna did not disclose any arrangements with Huber.
Sebastianelli's new annual base salary is $725,000, the company said. He earned $611,742 in salary last year.
His target annual bonus was not disclosed.

If he is not offered the top post, Sebastianelli's benefits would continue for three years, and he would be able to sell certain Aetna stock that he was awarded sooner than current restrictions allow.
Sebastianelli was co-president of Pennsylvania-based U.S. Healthcare before Aetna bought the company last July.
